title: the_recipe_box_incident
display_title: My MIL 'organized' my kitchen and threw out the one thing I can't replace
beats: My mother-in-law (61F) reorganized my kitchen while I was at work, and my grandmother's recipe box is gone.
Not misplaced. Gone. She said it was 'just an old rusty tin full of stained cards' and put it out for the garbage truck.
That box had my grandmother's handwriting in it. She died four years ago. There are no copies.
I called the waste company that afternoon, shaking. Truck already compacted, dispatcher said, nothing to be done.
I told my MIL what she threw away. She said, and I quote, 'You should scan things if they're that important.'
My husband (31M) says she was trying to help and I need to let it go since 'it's just paper.' His sister says I'm being dramatic over a tin box.
I haven't spoken to my MIL in nine days, and I told my husband if she's not banned from my kitchen going forward, I'm done cooking family dinners at our house. So, Reddit... AITAH?
